quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a green light. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to frighten them so they won't cross against a red light again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
Signal and enter. Other traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly so you can watch the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, signal and match the speed of other vehicles. Always let existing traffic go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: T intersection ahead.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming. Be ready to turn left or right.

questions.question: Can you avoid a traffic signal by driving on public or private property?

options.text: No, under no circumstances.
Yes, if the property owner gives you permission.
Yes, if you are running late.
Yes, if a police officer directs you to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a police officer directs you to do so.
questions.explanation: Driving on public or private property to avoid a traffic signal or sign is illegal. The only exception is if a police officer directs you to do so.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There are more vehicles on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so you cannot see as well as during the day. You must use your headlights from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

questions.question: What happens if you break the rules of a Graduated Driver License?

options.text: It is not a serious problem.
You will only get points on your license.
Nothing bad will happen.
You may have to pay a fine and your license may be suspended.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to pay a fine and your license may be suspended.
questions.explanation: New drivers with a Graduated Driver License must follow strict rules. Breaking these rules can result in a $100 fine and loss of your license.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Mistakes by drivers
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Mistakes by drivers
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when a driver doesn't see another vehicle or does something unexpected. Talk with other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: If you take a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Read the labels on the drug.
Drink alcohol instead.
Ignore any warning labels and drive anyway.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings about effects on driving. This includes cold and allergy medicine. If you have questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Look through your back window for people and objects before backing up. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially with children near. Get out and check behind your car before backing up or out of a driveway.

questions.question: When you must stop at an intersection but there are no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Slow down to make sure traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can clearly see traffic approaching before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see traffic approaching before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest point to the intersection where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they plan to stop. If you are following this driver, be prepared to slow down.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in residential areas unless a sign shows otherwise?

options.text: 10 mph.
25 mph.
45 mph.
65 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in residential areas is 25 mph. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing on the left is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green traffic light?

options.text: Keep driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you can proceed, but first check that no vehicles or pedestrians are still in the intersection. Be ready to slow down if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: When should you turn on your headlights?

options.text: 30 minutes after sunset.
30 minutes after sunrise.
When parked at a school.
When stopped at a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 minutes after sunset.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise. Also use them when windshield wipers are on due to rain or snow, or when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is driving aggressively?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Follow close behind them as payback.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make hand gestures.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light require you to do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal early, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the yellow light appears, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After completing the turn, where should your car be?

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your hazard lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: What must you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. Stop completely and look for pedestrians and traffic before going through the intersection.

questions.question: What is the Implied Consent Law?

options.text: Permission to let someone else drive your vehicle.
A requirement to wear seat belts.
Drivers agree to take a breath test if arrested for drunk driving.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers agree to take a breath test if arrested for drunk driving.
questions.explanation: By driving on the road, you agree to take a breath test if you are arrested for drinking and driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital is located to the right.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and be careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely.
Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden under the seat.
To stop the seat belt warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit a fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes, then back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. Go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols show construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is true for drivers under 21 with a probationary license?

options.text: They can use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
They cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
They should not wear a seat belt.
They can use a hand-held cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Probationary drivers have special rules. They cannot use any cell phone while driving and must wear a seat belt. Drivers under 21 cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas. Do not brake until you have control. Then brake gently and pull over safely.

questions.question: If you drive with a suspended license and cause an accident that injures someone, what happens?

options.text: You will get a warning.
You will only pay a fine.
You may pay a fine, get a longer suspension, and go to jail.
You will get points on your license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pay a fine, get a longer suspension, and go to jail.
questions.explanation: Driving with a suspended license is illegal. You will pay a fine, go to jail for up to 45 days, and get a longer license suspension.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or ice appears. These create slippery roads. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: A driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give that vehicle more space.
Know that this driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not copy this driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because accidents are more likely.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches, even if lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop while the red lights flash and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what else should you do after setting the parking brake?

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels away from the curb. If the car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before turning right. Do not cut across lanes to make a turn.

questions.question: If another car is coming toward you with bright headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright headlights and toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded until the car passes.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than the flow of traffic.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left, who do you have to yield the right-of-way to?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: What are the allowed driving hours for someone with a learner permit?

options.text: Between 12:01 a.m. and 5 a.m.
Between 9 a.m. and 9 p.m.
Between 5 a.m. and 11 p.m.
Anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between 5 a.m. and 11 p.m.
questions.explanation: Drivers with a learner permit cannot drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m.

questions.question: You see a crossbuck sign at a railroad crossing but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for a train.
Only cross when a flagger signals you to proceed, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Follow all instructions from a flagger if one is present.

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is not safe.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is not safe.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stop before entering the intersection when the light turns yellow, if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is showing red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is showing green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Road hazard sign.
Interstate route sign.
School crossing sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard sign.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are usually yellow and warn of hazards or special rules. Orange diamond signs are used in work areas.
